- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment drops below 0.3 or shows negative spikes, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% to account for risk reversal or market panic.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak.  
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive downward moves), model tends to lag; add 1–3% lagged correction to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early sentiment-driven reversals; apply a 1–2 day lagged sentiment filter to adjust forecast direction.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model often overfits to recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce volatility weight by 30%.
